samples.summary: Unrequested scope: share links are now polled every 60s and a live shared session is evicted to "Link unavailable" on failure
samples.evidence: The originating work is issue #1045 (select-all + type must be one undo unit). This hunk replaces the one-shot `resolveShareLink` effect with `useQuery({ refetchInterval: SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS, refetchOnWindowFocus: true, staleTime: 0, retry: 1 })`, and the render branch is `if (!token || error || !resolved)`. Because react-query sets `error` on a *background* refetch failure while `data` is still cached, two failed resolve attempts (a transient API blip, a proxy hiccup, an offline moment) tear a working shared editing session down to the "Link unavailable" screen, discarding the mounted editor, caret and scroll state. That is a user-visible product behaviour change — periodic network traffic per open tab plus session eviction — that no part of the undo-granularity issue asks for and no design doc records. It also silently changes the semantics documented in docs/design/sharing.md ("Revocation — Deleting a ShareLink immediately invalidates the token" is now "within ~60s for an open tab").

samples.summary: Share-link revalidation and editor write-authority revocation are an architecture change to sharing, but docs/design/sharing.md is untouched
samples.evidence: sharing.md is the canonical doc for share-link roles and for the client-side read-only write boundary (lines 163-219: "the client-side `readOnly` flag is the write boundary rather than a convenience in front of one… `EditorAPI`'s store and doc accessors hand out a neutered `DocStore` under `readOnly` (packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts, issue #989)"). This change adds (a) periodic token re-resolution with a new `SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS` constant, (b) editor rebuild on a mid-session `editor`→`viewer` downgrade in docs/notes/slides, (c) a whole new revocation mechanism — `revocableDocStore`, `EditorAPI.isDisposed()`, `neuterMutations` on dispose, `pasteContent`/`pastePlainTextFromClipboard` disposal guards, `YorkieDocStore.dispose()`. Only docs/design/docs/docs-collaboration.md was updated, and only for the undo work; the sharing design doc still describes a role that is fixed at page load and a read-only boundary decided solely at construction. CONTRIBUTING expects the canonical subsystem doc to be updated for an architecture change.

samples.summary: NotesView now remounts on `readOnly` change but its store is never disposed, unlike the docs path that added `store.dispose()` for exactly this
samples.evidence: The docs hunk adds `store.dispose()` in the cleanup with the rationale "a store left subscribed would keep handling remote-change… for the editor this cleanup just disposed", and `YorkieDocStore` gained `dispose()`; slides already had `store.dispose()` (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/slides-view.tsx:1216). `YorkieNoteStore` subscribes in its constructor (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:143) and exposes no `dispose()`, and NotesView's cleanup only does `storeRef.current = null`. Adding `readOnly` to the deps means every downgrade leaves a live `doc.subscribe` handler owned by a dead store (its `captureHistorySelection` keeps running for the whole document lifetime). The fix pattern already exists in two sibling packages and was not applied here.

samples.summary: `MemDocStore.batch()` now diverges from `MemSlidesStore.batch()` while its comment still claims to mirror it
samples.evidence: The retained comment says "Mirrors `MemSlidesStore.batch()`", but this change gives MemDocStore checkpoint *adoption* and moves redo clearing from `snapshot()` to a per-write `willWrite()`. `packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts:1789-1793` still does the simple `undoStack.push(clone(this.doc)); this.redoStack = []` at batch entry. Two near-identical in-memory undo stores now answer differently for the `snapshot(); batch(…)` ordering and for redo invalidation, with no note of the divergence in either place — the classic shape of duplicated logic that drifts.

samples.summary: The #1045 outcome is only partly delivered: toolbar/find-replace multi-write actions still lose content past the 50-entry cap
samples.evidence: The new doc text itself states: "`toggleList` / `indent` / `outdent` / `applyBlockStyle` and the cell-range style loop — and `FindReplaceState.replaceAll()` still issue an unbatched write per block (per *match*, twice, for Replace All), so on a selection larger than the 50-entry cap they lose their oldest writes exactly as the keyboard paths did before #1045." If the issue's acceptance is "no user action can overflow the undo cap and lose content", it is unmet for these paths; if it is scoped to select-all-then-type, this is fine and the #1048 tracking note suffices. Flagged so the gap is weighed rather than assumed out of scope — `withUndoUnit` was placed on `TextEditor`, which structurally cannot cover the `EditorAPI` toolbar paths.

samples.summary: Disposal-time write revocation is implemented only for the docs editor, though the mid-session downgrade it defends against now applies to notes and slides too
samples.evidence: `revocableDocStore` + `isDisposed()` + `neuterMutations` exist only in packages/docs; NotesView and SlidesView now also rebuild on a `readOnly` flip (this diff) but their editors/stores keep the pre-#989-style construction-time gate with no revocation of handles or async continuations. The stale-holder hazard the docs comments describe (an in-flight upload or clipboard read resuming on the pre-downgrade editor) is not obviously docs-specific, so the fix is asymmetric across the three packages the change touches.

samples.summary: Three stacked proxies over one store is heavy for the stated need
samples.evidence: `revocableDocStore` implements ten traps (including `getPrototypeOf`/`preventExtensions`/`ownKeys` invariant handling) and a memoized bind cache, and is then wrapped again by `pageSetupGuardedStore`, on top of `readOnlyDocStore`. The requirement — "stop writing after dispose" — could be met by a single flag checked in the existing read-only wrapper's factory. Taste-level, but the proxy layering is now a non-obvious identity/prototype surface for every store consumer.

finding.summary: Unrequested scope: share links are now polled every 60s and a live shared session is evicted to "Link unavailable" on failure
finding.evidence: The originating work is issue #1045 (select-all + type must be one undo unit). This hunk replaces the one-shot `resolveShareLink` effect with `useQuery({ refetchInterval: SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS, refetchOnWindowFocus: true, staleTime: 0, retry: 1 })`, and the render branch is `if (!token || error || !resolved)`. Because react-query sets `error` on a *background* refetch failure while `data` is still cached, two failed resolve attempts (a transient API blip, a proxy hiccup, an offline moment) tear a working shared editing session down to the "Link unavailable" screen, discarding the mounted editor, caret and scroll state. That is a user-visible product behaviour change — periodic network traffic per open tab plus session eviction — that no part of the undo-granularity issue asks for and no design doc records. It also silently changes the semantics documented in docs/design/sharing.md ("Revocation — Deleting a ShareLink immediately invalidates the token" is now "within ~60s for an open tab").

verdict.reason: Verified in-tree. shared-document.tsx:1107-1119 is exactly the described useQuery (refetchInterval SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS=60_000 at line 88, refetchOnWindowFocus, staleTime 0, retry 1), and line 1125's `if (!token || error || !resolved)` routes to the "Link unavailable" screen (line 1132) with no `isError && !data` narrowing or cached-data fallback — under @tanstack/react-query ^5.74.4 (package.json:56) a failed background refetch populates `error` while `data` remains, so the eviction path is reachable in a live session. The scope claim also checks out: the originating issue's todo (20260907-docs-select-all-type-undo-todo.md, Goal line 22-25, Plan lines 29-47) is entirely undo-granularity work and mentions no share-link behavior, while the companion lessons file (lines 54-70, 85-87) confirms the interval revalidation rode along with this change and that "polling after the error page" and the "sharing.md revalidation contract" were deliberately left unaddressed. docs/design/sharing.md:198 still documents immediate revocation with no revalidation contract recorded. Unrequested scope creep is explicitly in the design-fit lane, and the cost (periodic per-tab traffic plus eviction of a mounted editor with caret/scroll state on sustained failure) lands outside codebase tidiness, so it is not out-of-scope, not-present, or already-guarded.

searchedFor: read editor.ts readOnly branch and dispose()
finding.summary: Disposal revokes only the `EditorAPI` methods, not the live `getStore()` / `getDoc()` handles — the same gap #989 closed for `readOnly` has no counterpart here
finding.evidence: `dispose()` sets `disposed` and calls `neuterMutations(api)`, and the `EditorAPI.isDisposed` doc comment claims "A disposed editor is inert — every mutating method has been neutered". The read-only branch's own comment (editor.ts, `if (readOnly)`) explains that a name allowlist cannot guard handles it merely returns, and that `getStore()`/`getDoc()` are covered instead by `readOnlyDocStore` (#989). Under disposal there is no such coverage: a stale holder that captured the API before an `editor`→`viewer` downgrade can still call `api.getStore().insertText(...)` or write through `api.getDoc()` on a non-readOnly-built editor, which is exactly the escape route this delta claims disposal closes. Existing callers do reach the document that way (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-find-bar.tsx:66-67 drives find/replace through `getDoc()`/`getStore()`), so the boundary the change asserts is not the boundary it implements.

verdict.reason:
The claimed gap does not exist: disposal revokes the live store/doc handles, not just the `EditorAPI` method names.

Counterexample chain, all in the working tree:

1. `packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:190-229` defines `revocableDocStore(store, isRevoked)` — a Proxy that forwards while `isRevoked()` is false and becomes a `readOnlyDocStore` (all mutators no-op, prototype nulled, set/defineProperty/deleteProperty/setPrototypeOf refused) the moment it answers true. Its doc comment states exactly the reviewer's concern and says the handle itself must go dead because `docs-find-bar` captures both once for the editor's lifetime.
2. `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1138-1140`: `const revocableStore = readOnly ? docStore : revocableDocStore(docStore, () => disposed);` and `const doc = new Doc(readStore)` where `readStore` is that revocable store for a non-readOnly editor. So the single `Doc` handed out by `getDoc()` writes through the revocable store.
3. `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3309` `pageSetupGuardedStore` is a Proxy over `revocableStore`, and `getStore()` (line 3339) returns it for non-readOnly editors; its `setPageSetup` override (line 3307) also routes through `revocableStore`.
4. `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4475-4476` `dispose()` sets `disposed = true` before `neuterMutations(api)`, which flips the `isRevoked` closure and kills every copy of the handle already captured.

So `api.getStore().insertText(...)` and writes through `api.getDoc()` on a disposed, non-readOnly-built editor are no-ops, which is precisely the escape route the finding says is unguarded. Comments at editor.ts:1128-1139, 3333-3339 and 4539-4543 describe this as the deliberate disposal counterpart to the #989 read-only coverage. The reviewer's own quoted comment at the `if (readOnly)` branch (4539-4546) in fact says "Disposal covers the same two the same way — `revocableDocStore` turns into a `readOnlyDocStore` the moment `disposed` flips."
